advice: Gate new capabilities on the 8-criterion rubric: unknowable-from-weights, live/exact, obvious trigger, few args, verifiable answer, fast, no auth, no UI.
detail: Reference tool (domain availability) passes 8/8. Score every candidate vertical before building; experiments that fail 3+ criteria are research, not products.

advice: Run fixed corpora across app/tool/description variants and bank per-variant selection rates — first run recorded 2026-09-13.
detail: registry/experiments.json defines variants; `studio experiment` runs them via the similarity proxy and writes registry/results/. B-availability/C-finder tied 0.80, A-checker 0.67 on run one. Re-run with model judge before submission decisions.

advice: Run the closed loop as SOP: real usage failures → new eval cases → candidate metadata → routing benchmark → ship winner.
detail: Operational form of Casey's hill-climbing. Every metadata edit (name, description, subtitle, schema, param wording) must move measured precision/recall before shipping.

advice: Maintain explicit should-NOT-trigger evals per vertical — review demands them and selection quality needs them.
detail: Submission bar is 5 positive + 3 negative minimum; our bar should be thousands. Starter pairs: boiler repair request vs how-boilers-work; domain availability vs why-.coms-valuable; hoodie order vs what-is-DTG. Track P(tool|irrelevant) alongside recall.

advice: Standardize evals per router as six JSONL files: positives, negatives, ambiguous, tool_selection, parameter_extraction, ranking.
detail: Seed volumes: domains ~5k utterances, trades 10k+. CI reports precision, recall, false-positive rate, parameter accuracy. This file set is a candidate internal moat.

advice: Generate candidate tool descriptions with the model, then benchmark the model's own routing on them — interfaces optimized by their consumer.
detail: Casey's 'models are fairly good at writing for themselves'. Concretes: prompt GPT for 5 description variants per tool, score each on the eval set, keep the winner. Re-run when base models change.

advice: Enforce p95 <1s for cached discovery, <2s for fresh lookups; never block a synchronous tool on humans — split RFQ into request/get.
detail: Community best-practice consensus + our plan: search returns immediately, request_* creates async work, get_* polls. Our domains live RDAP already measures ~100–400ms, inside budget.
